trials.notes: Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for BODY-fragment structure, then a single next_token() walk bounded by get_current_depth(). All HTML API calls used by the candidate are documented in the rendered files: create_fragment, next_tag, next_token, get_current_depth, get_token_type, get_token_name, is_tag_closer, and get_modifiable_text. It also followed the documented ordinary-text pattern by reading get_modifiable_text() only from #text tokens. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Correctly chose the structural HTML Processor rather than the lexical Tag Processor, bounded traversal to the first TABLE subtree by recorded depth, and collected only decoded #text tokens. All called HTML API methods are documented: create_fragment, next_tag, next_token, get_current_depth, get_token_type, get_tag, is_tag_closer, and get_modifiable_text. No hallucinated calls or _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 8 frozen cases, so there are no failed hidden cases to attribute to documentation gaps. The docs did well on the key decisions this task required: the Tag Processor overview explicitly says to use WP_HTML_Processor when structure, subtree walking, implied/missing closers, or text collection matters; HTML Processor next_token() explains that it visits text, implied table structure, and virtual closers; get_current_depth() documents the >= depth-bound pattern; and get_modifiable_text() warns that ordinary DOM-style text extraction should first require get_token_type() === '#text' and that returned #text is already decoded. The main near-miss is that the needed solution is assembled from several sections: processor choice, depth-bounded subtree walking, repeated-region state machines, and decoded text semantics. The subjects assembled those pieces correctly here.

doc_gaps.problem: The ingredients for repeated-region extraction are documented, but split across separate examples: one shows a depth-bounded subtree walk and another shows a one-pass state machine for repeated items. A reader has to combine them for cases like collecting repeated child regions inside one selected container.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general, non-table-specific recipe that selects a container, records its depth, walks once with a >= depth guard, and tracks repeated child elements with state variables, for example extracting DT/DD or LI text from a selected list.

doc_gaps.problem: The decoded-text contract is present, but it is easy to miss because it sits in prose after the broader definition of modifiable text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Promote the key read contract into a short return-note bullet: for #text, TITLE, and TEXTAREA, returned text is already decoded UTF-8; do not html_entity_decode() it again; empty string is not proof that the token is an ordinary text node.
